faqs.q: How is wildlife removal priced in Portsmouth?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing and cleanup the job needs. Our crew inspects first, shows you the entry points we found in Portsmouth, and gives you a quote after inspection before any removal or sealing work begins — no prices promised over the phone.

faqs.q: Why are rats such a steady problem in Portsmouth?
faqs.a: Norway rats — and roof rats in warmer coastal housing — follow food, water, and foundation gaps, and in Portsmouth those three sit close together. Rats travel between neighboring buildings, so our crew pairs trapping with sealing foundation, sewer, and utility entries; treating one house without sealing it usually means rats return from next door. Any pesticide work is separate VDACS-certified work, not part of a wildlife permit.

Portsmouth.wildlife_intro:
Portsmouth's dense historic neighborhoods across from Norfolk are older-housing rat and raccoon country in Portsmouth. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: elizabeth River's western branch, Olde Towne's historic blocks, shipyard waterfront. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Portsmouth — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
